searchText: Hey all. Wondering what others are using to check for peer liveness? Libp2p has a ping protocol, but it's not spec'd for eth2. We were using that but are thinking of potentially using STATUS to act as the ping. Curious what others are using? technically, if you're gossiping with the peer, can't you make an assumption about traffic / bytes on wire and some timeout? Sure. But couldn't we have peers that are not on any of our subscribed topics, so won't receive traffic? I guess we should get at least get gossip on the main channels Prysm fetches status from all connected peers periodically, and drops them if they don't respond That's actually a bit of a problem in libp2p, there is no way of actively detect dead peers, as <@498009160982724610> has noted. Status could work, but it might be too heavy for that. ^ I was thinking this. Also we haven't really discussed the option of peers supporting gossip and not rpc One way of doing it, is to have a ping when the peer has been silent for some time in order to not to spam the peer too heavyly Yeah, so the question becomes, do we use a seperate protocol, or try use one of the ones we have specd I think a separate protocol is more flexible, how heavy is the status message and do you have to send it periodically, if yes then that could work If not, I'd say it probably end up being too chatty Fetching status periodically is useful for us as we use the information from it to decide who to sync against if we fall behind. And if a fork occurred we would use it to drop peers that are on a different fork How often do you status? Is it a fixed time or dependent on some peer heuristic? *Think* it's twice an epoch but not 100% on that Yeah cool thanks. I think I'll adopt this approach for the time being, unless we decide to do a ping-like protocol

excerpts.author: agemanning
excerpts.content:
Hey all. Wondering what others are using to check for peer liveness? 
Libp2p has a ping protocol, but it's not spec'd for eth2. We were using that but are thinking of potentially using STATUS to act as the ping. 
Curious what others are using?

excerpts.author: arnetheduck
excerpts.content: technically, if you're gossiping with the peer, can't you make an assumption about traffic / bytes on wire and some timeout?

excerpts.author: agemanning
excerpts.content: Sure. But couldn't we have peers that are not on any of our subscribed topics, so won't receive traffic?

excerpts.author: agemanning
excerpts.content: I guess we should get at least get gossip on the main channels

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content: Prysm fetches status from all connected peers periodically, and drops them if they don't respond

excerpts.author: dryajov
excerpts.content: That's actually a bit of a problem in libp2p, there is no way of actively detect dead peers, as <@498009160982724610> has noted. Status could work, but it might be too heavy for that.

excerpts.author: agemanning
excerpts.content:
^ I was thinking this. 
Also we haven't really discussed the option of peers supporting gossip and not rpc

excerpts.author: dryajov
excerpts.content: One way of doing it, is to have a ping when the peer has been silent for some time in order to not to spam the peer too heavyly

excerpts.author: agemanning
excerpts.content: Yeah, so the question becomes, do we use a seperate protocol, or try use one of the ones we have specd

excerpts.author: dryajov
excerpts.content: I think a separate protocol is more flexible, how heavy is the status message and do you have to send it periodically, if yes then that could work

excerpts.author: dryajov
excerpts.content: If not, I'd say it probably end up being too chatty

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content: Fetching status periodically is useful for us as we use the information from it to decide who to sync against if we fall behind.  And if a fork occurred we would use it to drop peers that are on a different fork

excerpts.author: agemanning
excerpts.content: How often do you status? Is it a fixed time or dependent on some peer heuristic?

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content: *Think* it's twice an epoch but not 100% on that

excerpts.author: agemanning
excerpts.content: Yeah cool thanks. I think I'll adopt this approach for the time being, unless we decide to do a ping-like protocol
